comparator.name: Biomedical Engineering
comparator.sourceNotes: The 2026–2027 Biomedical Engineering after-revision PER Articles 3.3–3.5 and Appendix 2, and generation-2026 chart (2026–2027, 2027–2028, 2028–2029), were freshly retrieved and inspected on 8 October 2026. Instruction is Dutch and English, correcting normalized ENG-only metadata while preserving raw ENG provenance. This is the BBT Biomedical Engineering programme, not the alternative MWT Medical Sciences and Technology core. Current core 125 EC includes 110 taught/project EC and 8FINAL Bachelor Final Project 15; ITEC is 10 and genuine free space 45, replacing the older 105/15/15/45 allocation. Year one is 55 core + 5 ITEC (60); year two 40 core + 20 electives (60); year three 15 taught core + 5 ITEC + 15 project + 25 electives (60). Skills Experience 8BA050 spans two 5-EC quarter positions and is counted once at 10 EC. Personal and Professional Development is embedded in existing core/CBL credits; mandatory MyFuture activities and five Studium Generale activities for ITEC carry no separately added credit here. The 45 free EC require at least 30 EC at levels 2/3, including at least 15 at level 3; external courses require approval and degree-content overlap must be avoided. Pink diagram examples are recommendations; MWT-only core such as Mechanobiology and Cancer Cell Biology is not added as universal BBT formation. Required BBT Materials Science remains included. For 8BA020, the current cohort diagram and official TU/e course profile use Engineering organs on a chip; the formal PER uses Engineering a Tissue. The component retains this title variation explicitly at the same code, required CBL role and 5 EC, without asserting a formal PER amendment. NAC 8BB070 is retained without an unsupported acronym expansion. BEP admission requires at least 120 completed credits including compulsory first-year components, all year-one/two P&PD skills, eight year-two/three core units including two year-two CBLs, and four year-two/three elective units. Results in the immediately preceding examination period do not count for this entry check, and interim results do not count for a Q1 start. The interdisciplinary challenge requires prior participation in the offered units embedding communication, cooperation, planning and organizing (8BA020/8BA050). No duplicate skills, route alternatives or optional biomedical examples adds credits. Fresh1November2026 verifies all26 positions180EC and formal rules from adoptedPER/currentgeneration2026chart. Ordinary BEP is a15EC block in year3Q4; completing the firsttwo years gives120EC including firstyear,8year2coreunits with2CBLs and4year2electives, already available before the immediately preceding year3Q3exam period. P&PD completion remains separately required. PERArt3.7:submit180ECplan after45ECearned viaPlanApp, board assesses choices and changes require approval. No external-course-only approval exception inferred. Latest samePER assessment table explicitly calls8BA020 Engineering organs on a chip, corroborating chart despite older label elsewhere. Current official2026course descriptions verify imaging includes processing as well as acquisition; clinical measurement centres sensors/signals; biostatistics centres applied regression/ANOVA. Anatomy alone is not clinical instrumentation. No core/route credits changed; sourceprofile retrieval403 does not block independently established identity/content.

routeSelection.basis: The normalized target is Biomedical Engineering rather than the separately normalized Medical Sciences and Technology target. Current PER Appendix2.2c formally lists these180EC specializations; public programme page distinguishes the technical BMT core from the more biological MWT core. Select the named technical core, not whichever matches UCR more easily.

core: Human biology, cells, biomolecules, physiology and experimental life science
Mathematical and computational modelling of biological and technical systems
Medical imaging and biomedical signal/image analysis
Statistics and machine learning for biomedical measurements
Patient-oriented healthcare technology and design projects
adjacent: Disease mechanisms, diagnosis, treatment and clinical translation

trace: develops customer-led product concepts, fabrication methods, prototypes, quantitative models and sustainability/cost analysis; this supports patient-oriented design work without claiming medical-device engineering These are the stated methods applicable to the concept; no biomedical dataset, patient brief or clinical hardware project is guaranteed.

implements search, constraint satisfaction and optimisation for complex biomedical-model and design problems These are the stated methods applicable to the concept; no biomedical dataset, patient brief or clinical hardware project is guaranteed.

develops algorithm and data-structure design with performance analysis for reproducible biomedical-data workflows These are the stated methods applicable to the concept; no biomedical dataset, patient brief or clinical hardware project is guaranteed.

provides data cleaning, manipulation, visualisation and project work for interpreting biomedical measurements These are the stated methods applicable to the concept; no biomedical dataset, patient brief or clinical hardware project is guaranteed.
applies regression and tree-based learning to real data, including documented medical examples
directly studies image feature detection, tracking and medical-image applications; it does not supply image-acquisition physics

develops neural-network and computer-vision models for advanced biomedical image/data analysis These are the stated methods applicable to the concept; no biomedical dataset, patient brief or clinical hardware project is guaranteed.

studies kinematics, motion planning and robotic manipulation as computational foundations for assistive or clinical systems, not biomedical hardware These are the stated methods applicable to the concept; no biomedical dataset, patient brief or clinical hardware project is guaranteed.
supplies structured programming, testing and debugging for scientific computation and biomedical-data analysis
Calculus, complex numbers, differential equations and dynamic-model analysis support quantitative physiological/system models.
develops matrix methods, linear transformations and eigenvalue reasoning for multivariable biomedical models
implements numerical equation solving, integration and differential equations for dynamic physiological models
extends calculus to several variables and differential equations for coupled biological processes
studies differential-equation, transfer-function and state-space representations relevant to physiological signals and systems
develops probability, estimation and simulation for biomedical measurements and model uncertainty
studies human structure/function through imaging, surface anatomy and dissection materials
connects molecular drug targets and kinetics to therapeutic effects and toxicity
studies immune recognition, host-pathogen interactions, inflammation and tissue damage

Direct disease-context contribution: integrate normal organ function, symptoms, pathophysiology, diagnostic findings, treatment and prognosis across organ systems, with case analysis; not medical-device engineering.

Direct molecular/cellular biomedical foundation: biomolecules, membranes, communication, metabolism, heredity and gene expression, with scientific experiment/paper analysis; not a dedicated whole-organ physiology course.
introduces brain anatomy, injury and behaviour as a defined human-system application
directly studies prokaryotic and eukaryotic cell biology, current research and reproducibility
studies human structure/function, signalling, homeostasis, energy handling and integrated organ systems
studies biomolecule chemistry, metabolic pathways and their roles in health and disease
practises biochemical and molecular laboratory work with blood, proteins, bacteria, DNA and bioinformatics
studies mutations, genetic testing, cell injury, inflammation, repair and neoplasia
adds regression, multivariate inference, experimental design and applied analysis for biomedical research
develops systematic review, meta-analysis, effect-size calculation and bias assessment for evidence-based health research

alternatives.label: Biomedical imaging, modelling & data systems
alternatives.concept: Combine human biology and laboratory science with mathematical systems, programming, statistics, machine learning, medical-image analysis, computational robotics and product design. This is a biomedical-data and systems response, not a biomedical-device engineering substitute.
alternatives.labelReason: The schedule contains a cumulative biology/laboratory sequence and a cumulative mathematical, computational, imaging and design sequence; the label avoids claiming the absent mechanics, electronics and instrumentation formation.
progression: Consumer Product Design moved to its actual first-semester offering; Introductory Data Science moves to semester4 before Machine Learning in5. All other course placements retained. Every formal prerequisite precedes its dependent, actual offerings checked in all six fixed terms; no additional hard prerequisite invented.

alternatives.label: Human physiology, molecular disease & quantitative health
alternatives.concept: Retain human biology, laboratory work, physiology, mathematical models, statistics and medical-image analysis while prioritising pharmacology, immunity, disease mechanisms and evidence synthesis for diagnosis and treatment questions.
alternatives.labelReason: Five advanced computational courses are replaced by pharmacology, immunology, disease mechanisms, brain/behaviour foundations and health-evidence synthesis, producing a distinct biomedical-science route without a clinical or engineering claim.
progression: Consumer Product Design moved to its actual first-semester offering; Introductory Data Science moves to semester4 before Machine Learning in5. All other course placements retained. Every formal prerequisite precedes its dependent, actual offerings checked in all six fixed terms; no additional hard prerequisite invented.
alternatives.distinctness: Five courses / 37.5 EC differ in each direction. Algorithms, Robotics, Statistics & Experimental Methods, Optimisation and Deep Learning are replaced by Pharmacology, Infection & Immunity, Introduction to Brain & Behavior, Mechanisms of Disease and Advanced Research Seminar.

candidates.label: Physiology, disease mechanisms and clinical translation
Medical devices, biomechanics and tissue engineering

selection.assessment: Two complete related programmes pass the content, schedule and 30-EC distinctness gates. The first owns the integrated imaging/modelling/data direction; the second is independently supported by physiology, diagnosis, treatment and clinical-translation interests. A further device, biomechanics and tissue-engineering direction cannot supply tissue mechanics, biomaterials, sensors, circuits, instrumentation, clinical measurement hardware or tissue-engineering laboratories. General anatomy, robotics and product design cannot be relabelled as those subjects. No third programme is manufactured.

blocks: Both directly study molecular and cellular biology; UCR does not reproduce the complete engineering context.
Both directly study biomolecule chemistry and biochemical function.
Both establish calculus for quantitative scientific models.
Partial correspondence in matrices, vector spaces, linear transformations and systems. The TU/e component also includes multivariable calculus, which is studied separately at UCR.

Both directly study differential-equation, state-space, time/frequency and Laplace representations of dynamic systems. UCR focuses on signals and linear systems rather than the full range of physical biomedical examples.

Direct partial correspondence in experimental design, multivariable model fitting, group comparisons, categorical outcomes and assumption checks. UCR applies these methods to health and behavioural research; TU/e develops biomedical linear/logistic models and ANOVA.
Both establish programming and data methods for technical/scientific work.
Both teach core machine-learning methods; UCR retains its broader cross-domain framing.

Both directly teach filtering, image enhancement, segmentation and image-analysis methods. TU/e additionally requires the physics of medical acquisition and treatment modalities, which UCR computer vision does not reproduce.
Both use multidisciplinary product/design development; UCR concerns general consumer products rather than biomedical engineering integration.

The required component centres physical measurement chains, sensors and signal processing. Anatomy teaches structure and interpretation of medical images, rather than these measurement methods. Linear Systems supplies related sampling/Fourier/filtering methods but occupies the stronger Dynamic Systems row.

notes.text: The UCR alternatives combine biomedical science, laboratory work, quantitative modelling, image/data analysis and design, with either computational systems or molecular disease applications. They do not reproduce the target's physics, tissue mechanics, flow/diffusion, biomaterials, sensors, electronics, instrumentation, engineering projects or biomedical capstone.

audience.programmeDescription: Biomedical Engineering at TU/e combines biology, chemistry, physics, mathematics and computing to develop healthcare technologies. This Dutch- and English-taught pathway emphasises technical models, biomedical measurements, imaging, materials and engineering projects, alongside biological foundations and a final bachelor project.
audience.comparisonExplanation: The first UCR programme combines biomedical science and laboratory work with mathematical modelling, image and data analysis, and general product-design methods. The second places more weight on physiology, disease mechanisms and health evidence. These are related academic routes; they do not supply the specialist mechanics, instrumentation, biomaterials, tissue engineering and integrated healthcare-device projects of TU/e’s technical pathway.

curriculum.limitation: The 45 EC of electives remain open, subject to approval, prior knowledge, non-overlap and level requirements. Entry to the 15-EC final project requires at least 120 EC including compulsory first-year study, completed first- and second-year professional skills, eight later core courses including two second-year CBL projects, and four later elective courses. Results from the immediately preceding exam period do not count for entry.

componentNotes.8BA050: One required 10-EC skills component spanning two quarter positions, counted once.
componentNotes.8FINAL: Compulsory 15-EC final project in a block in the fourth quarter of year three. Entry includes credit, core-course, elective and professional-skills requirements; immediately preceding exam-period results are excluded.
componentNotes.cp-000262-y2-open-8: Part of the combined 45-EC free-elective space. At least 30 EC must be level two or three, including 15 EC at level three. The study plan requires approval and courses must not overlap the core or each other.
componentNotes.cp-000262-y3-open-5: Remaining 25 EC of the same elective space. Choices remain subject to approval, level, prior-knowledge and non-overlap conditions.
componentNotes.0LVX20: Five Studium Generale activities and MyFuture activities totalling value seven are additional non-credit obligations. Professional and personal development is embedded in credited components.
